scores.claim_text: Significant content on F-35, F-15, Blackhawk, Apache, guided tactical weapons.
supports: F-35: NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE at 2023 cutoff (corpus = FY26 PB); F-15: signal UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS but sparse history (FY2008 + FY2023 only, both $0 — clear coverage gap not a defunding signal); Blackhawk: NOT_FOUND; Apache: NOT_FOUND.
scores.M_value: F-35=NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE, F-15(F01500)=UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS but only 2 history rows (sparse), Blackhawk/Apache=NOT_FOUND
scores.interpretation: J-Book corpus is FY26 PB data — at PIT cutoff 2023-01-15 the cutoff_year filter excludes everything post-2023. Sparse FY2008+FY2023 zero-rows on F-15 variants do not reflect actual 2023 program funding (heuristic #3 and #7 apply: corpus reorganization / coverage gap). Mark UNVERIFIABLE; note Procurement-vs-RDT&E P-40 lines exist for F-15EX in the corpus but PIT 2023 view is non-discriminative.

scores.claim_text: U.S. Government direct + indirect sales = 23% FY2022, 29% FY2021.
supports: usaspending shows 850 DoD awards totaling $186.5M to Woodward, Inc. as of 2023-01-15 — confirms the company has real DoD revenue base.
scores.interpretation: USAspending confirms real, broad-based DoD contracting activity consistent with 23-29% government sales narrative. The trend (29% -> 23%) actually shows government share SHRINKING in FY22 vs FY21 — disclosed accurately. No J-Book contractor-name match (NOT_FOUND), but that's expected: Woodward is a sub-tier supplier, rarely a prime, so they don't appear as primary_contractors in J-Book exhibits.

scores.claim_text: Raytheon Technologies = 11% of consolidated net sales FY2022.
supports: edgar_fts: 1 hit for 'Woodward' in Raytheon (CIK 0000101829) filings pre-cutoff — counterparty disclosure exists but is minimal (Woodward is small relative to RTX).
scores.M_value: edgar_fts hits=1; jbook Raytheon contractor matches=2 PEs (Technology Maturation Initiatives, BMD Sensor Test) but NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE at 2023 cutoff
scores.interpretation: Customer concentration claim is internally verifiable from Woodward's own audited financials. Raytheon disclosure of Woodward is one-sided (small supplier), expected. The two J-Book PEs where Raytheon is a primary contractor are non-revenue-load-bearing for Woodward (Woodward is a sub-supplier on engines, not on BMD sensor tests). PASS.

scores.claim_text: GE = 11% of net sales FY2022, FY2021, FY2020 (split across Aerospace and Industrial).
supports: GE as a JV partner and customer is independently verifiable from segment narrative; LEAP and PurePower engine programs are commercial products with massive global production backlog.
scores.M_value: jbook NOT_FOUND for GE contractor; usaspending 'General Electric Aviation' literal string n=0 (need exact recipient form)
scores.interpretation: The GE concentration is primarily COMMERCIAL aerospace (LEAP engine = 737 MAX / A320neo) and INDUSTRIAL (heavy frame gas turbines), not DoD program element-driven. J-Book non-coverage is correct (LEAP is FAA-side, not Pentagon J-Book). Customer concentration is real and historically stable per the filing. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Woodward developed fuel system / air management / actuation for CFM LEAP engine and continues to support LEAP improvements.
supports: LEAP is a commercial engine program (737 MAX, A320neo, COMAC C919) — not a Pentagon J-Book program element. J-Book NOT_FOUND is correct/expected, not a divergence signal.
scores.interpretation: Non-J-Book claim by category — LEAP is commercial. NOT_FOUND is the correct null result. The forward-thesis is driven by Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo build rates, which are independently observable. PASS (no J-Book divergence).

scores.claim_text: Woodward supplies actuation/combustion/oil system components for Pratt & Whitney GTF (PurePower).
supports: Pratt & Whitney GTF is the A220 and A320neo (PW option) engine — commercial. Not a J-Book PE.
scores.interpretation: Same logic as C5 — commercial engine, expected NOT_FOUND in Pentagon J-Book. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Aerospace backlog $1.199B at Oct 31, 2022, 74% to be satisfied by Sep 30, 2023.
supports: usaspending confirms $186.5M of DoD obligations to Woodward (a fraction of total backlog — most is commercial OEM). Backlog conversion rate disclosed.
scores.interpretation: Backlog claim is a financial-disclosure number with clear timing schedule. usaspending corroborates DoD piece. PASS — no J-Book divergence available because Woodward is not a J-Book prime.

scores.claim_text: Products used on military fixed-wing aircraft, rotorcraft, guided weapons, and other defense systems (broad).
supports: Vague aggregate claim — no specific PE named. JASSM=NOT_FOUND, generic 'guided weapons'=NOT_FOUND.
scores.interpretation: The 10-K narrative does not name specific Program Elements or PE numbers. The 'guided tactical weapons' phrase is too generic to map to a J-Book line. Per heuristic #7, NOT_FOUND alone is not a red flag — the corpus may not cover the specific subsystem PEs Woodward supplies into. UNVERIFIABLE. This is an example of the *non-discriminative* disclosure style: the filing avoids PE-level commitments, which means the J-Book divergence test cannot fire.

scores.claim_text: Woodward owns numerous patents; US Govt has certain rights in govt-contract-derived patents.
supports: USPTO: 230 granted patents pre-cutoff, 586 total applications — substantial portfolio consistent with a 150-year-old aerospace controls company.
scores.interpretation: Patent portfolio is real and material; supports R&D and competitive-moat narrative. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Manufacturing/assembly plants primarily in US, Europe, Asia.
supports: EPA FRS Colorado lookup returned 8 facilities matching 'Woodward'. Headquarters Fort Collins, CO. Facility footprint confirmed at least in HQ state.

scores.claim_text: Raytheon Technologies discloses Woodward as a counterparty (reciprocal check).
supports: edgar_fts: total_hits=1 in Raytheon CIK 0000101829 filings — minimal reciprocal disclosure but expected given supplier asymmetry.
scores.interpretation: Low reciprocal disclosure is the expected pattern for a small supplier to a megacap defense prime — not a red flag. UNVERIFIABLE in the divergence-test sense (no inconsistency surfaced).

summary.framework_note: Woodward is a deep sub-tier supplier (fuel pumps, actuators, fuel nozzles) into commercial and defense engine OEMs (GE, P&W, Honeywell, RTX). The 10-K avoids naming specific Pentagon Program Elements. With no PE-level commitment in the narrative, the J-Book divergence test has nothing to discriminate against — the filing's disclosure granularity is too coarse. This is the OPPOSITE failure mode of the YSS/IONQ case: not a company hiding bad J-Book exposure, but a company whose forward thesis depends on COMMERCIAL aerospace cycle (LEAP, GTF, 787) and broad DoD aftermarket sustainment, neither of which the J-Book corpus is built to evaluate. No divergence pattern detected. Cohort framework correctly returns mostly PASS / UNVERIFIABLE — no false red flags.
